To fly directly from Uganda to Zaire was impossible because 
the shaky Zairean government, fighting for control of the counÂ­
try, had closed all international airports, and driving overland 
was not advised because of discouraging reports about bandits 
and guerrillas.

text: And so we had decided to fly south from Uganda into Burundi, then drive a rented van through Burundi and Rwanda, and on into eastern Zaire.

text: But Burundi was not at peace either.

Half a dozen waves of

text: In one month in 1972, Tutsis killed nearly every Hutu leader and any other Hutu who appeared literate.
text_raw:
In 
one month in 1972, Tutsis killed nearly every Hutu leader and 
any other Hutu who appeared literate.

text: Tutsis, though they acÂ­ counted for only about 15 percent of the populace, thus during the next two decades controlled the civil service, the military, and, within a one-party system, the upper reaches of governÂ­ ment.

counted for only about 15 percent of the populace, thus during

text: Until 1993, when the country experimented with demoÂ­ cratic, multiparty elections for the first time in history, every president had come from the minority Tutsis.

text: The June 1993 elections produced Burundi's first Hutu presiÂ­ dent, a political moderate, a believer in nonviolence and ethnic reconciliation, Melchior Ndadaye.

text: But in the early morning of October 21, 1993, four months before we paid for our visas, an army tank rammed a hole in the white stucco wall of the presidential palace and radical Tutsi soldiers stabbed President Ndadaye to death with a knife.
